headline: NCP reshuffles top leadership, retains Nahid Islam as convener
summary: Nasiruddin Patwary and Hasnat Abdullah are promoted, while Sarjis Alam and Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain move to lower-ranking positions.
details: The National Citizen Party (NCP), formed by student leaders of the 2024 mass uprising, has reshuffled its top leadership.
Nasiruddin Patwary and Hasnat Abdullah have been promoted in the party hierarchy, while Sarjis Alam and Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain have been placed in lower-ranking positions.
Sarjis, formerly the chief organiser for the northern region, and Asif, the party's spokesperson, are now senior joint member secretaries.
Nahid Islam remains the party's convener, and Akhter Hossen retains his post as member secretary.
The reshuffle comes nearly two years after the NCP's formation, and the party has yet to hold its first national council.

caption:
The National Citizen Party reshuffles its top brass. Who moves up and who moves down?

The National Citizen Party (NCP), formed by student leaders of the 2024 mass uprising, has reshuffled its top leadership.

Nasiruddin Patwary and Hasnat Abdullah have been promoted in the party hierarchy, while Sarjis Alam and Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain have been placed in lower-ranking positions.

Sarjis, formerly the chief organiser for the northern region, and Asif, the party's spokesperson, are now senior joint member secretaries.

Nahid Islam remains the party's convener, and Akhter Hossen retains his post as member secretary.

The reshuffle comes nearly two years after the NCP's formation, and the party has yet to hold its first national council.

Additionally, Samantha Sharmin has been moved from senior joint convenor to joint convenor.

Sharmin, a prominent leader since the July Uprising, did not contest the February 12 parliamentary election due to the party's alliance with Jamaat-e-Islami.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, bdnews24.com, Prothom Alo

headline_marked: 7,500 Bangladeshis [[held in Saudi prisons]], says State Minister
headline: 7,500 Bangladeshis held in Saudi prisons, says State Minister
summary: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam reveals the scale of Bangladeshi detainees in Saudi Arabia while receiving the body of a citizen killed in a missile strike.
details: Around 7,500 Bangladeshis are currently being held in prisons across Saudi Arabia, according to State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam.

The revelation was made during a press briefing at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka, following the arrival of the body of Mohammad Shahed Ahmed, who was killed in a missile strike in Saudi Arabia.
The government is coordinating with Saudi authorities to extend visas and iqamas for expatriates who cannot return to their workplaces due to ongoing conflict in the region.
Additionally, the government is discussing the rehabilitation and re-employment of Bangladeshi nationals who have lost their jobs abroad.
Regarding the recent execution of two Bangladeshis in Saudi Arabia, the State Minister stated that the government has not yet received detailed information on the cases.
The Bangladesh government has formally requested copies of the verdicts from Saudi authorities to establish the facts of these executions.
Minister Shama Obaed emphasized that while Bangladesh cannot interfere in another country's judicial system, it is the government's responsibility to assist its citizens abroad.
The government continues its efforts to gather more information regarding the legal cases involving Bangladeshi detainees.
caption:
7,500 Bangladeshis are currently imprisoned in Saudi Arabia, according to the State Minister for Foreign Affairs.

Around 7,500 Bangladeshis are currently being held in prisons across Saudi Arabia, according to State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam.

The revelation was made during a press briefing at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka, following the arrival of the body of Mohammad Shahed Ahmed, who was killed in a missile strike in Saudi Arabia.

The government is coordinating with Saudi authorities to extend visas and iqamas for expatriates who cannot return to their workplaces due to ongoing conflict in the region.

Additionally, the government is discussing the rehabilitation and re-employment of Bangladeshi nationals who have lost their jobs abroad.

Regarding the recent execution of two Bangladeshis in Saudi Arabia, the State Minister stated that the government has not yet received detailed information on the cases.

The Bangladesh government has formally requested copies of the verdicts from Saudi authorities to establish the facts of these executions.

Minister Shama Obaed emphasized that while Bangladesh cannot interfere in another country's judicial system, it is the government's responsibility to assist its citizens abroad.

The government continues its efforts to gather more information regarding the legal cases involving Bangladeshi detainees.

Source: The Daily Star, Dhaka Tribune, Prothom Alo
